Work in /opt/nxeon on a live Proxmox host. Your job: **rehearse the server-migration engine end to end against throwaway infrastructure, and report what actually breaks.** This is the flagship feature — the owner's stated reason customers will switch to Nxeon — and its verification gate has NEVER run against a real migration. Every bug found so far was discovered by a real customer domain going dark.

READ FIRST: `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` (28 numbered real failures), and in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` the three migration chapters plus "Known gaps".

WHAT YOU ARE ALLOWED TO DO — this is the unusual part, read carefully:
- You MAY create throwaway VMs on this Proxmox host and migrate between them. Use vmid **9500–9599** (well clear of templates 9000–9009 and customer VMs 100–199). Name them `rehearsal-src-*` / `rehearsal-dst-*`.
- You MAY install packages, write files and run services INSIDE those throwaway VMs freely.
- You MAY read the live database. You may create a Migration row and a MIGRATE Job **only** if both source and target are your own rehearsal VMs — never a customer's.
- You MUST NOT touch any VM outside 9500–9599, any customer row, any real domain's DNS, or the platform's own services. Do NOT restart nxeon-web or nxeon-worker.
- Clean up: destroy your rehearsal VMs when done. Report anything you could not clean.

THE REHEARSAL — build a source VM that resembles a real customer's box, because the gate's whole purpose is catching the messy cases:
1. A source with: nginx serving 2+ vhosts on real hostnames, a MySQL/MariaDB database with data, a Docker Compose project, a systemd unit whose `ExecStart` points at a hand-installed interpreter path (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/node`) that will NOT exist on the target — field-note item 13, which recurred after being documented. Add a `/var/www/html/index.html` that is Apache's default page.
2. A blank target VM from a template.
3. Run the real engine end to end.
4. Record precisely: what the gate caught, what it MISSED, whether `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` was set correctly, whether the served/total denominator was honest, whether default-page and cert-mismatch detection fired, and whether the `ExecStart` pre-flight resolved or blocked the bad unit.

WHAT I MOST WANT TO KNOW: does the gate report the truth? A migration that copies everything and says so is a pass. A migration that leaves something dark and SAYS SO is also a pass. A migration that leaves something dark and reports success is the failure mode that matters, and it is what shipped to a customer twice this week.

Note `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION=1` is set on this host, so the real engine will run. The worker is strictly serial — your MIGRATE job will block other jobs while it runs, so check the queue is empty first and keep the rehearsal tight.

REPORT: a numbered list of every defect found, each with file:line and a reproduction; whether the gate's honesty held; and any field-note item that has silently regressed. Write your findings to `docs/MIGRATION-REHEARSAL.md` (yours alone). Do NOT edit engine code — this is a test, not a fix; report so the fixes can be done deliberately.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT run `npm run build`/`npm run dev`, do NOT restart platform services, do NOT git commit/push, do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma or any file under lib/ worker/ app/ components/.
- If you cannot complete the rehearsal safely, stop and report why rather than improvising against customer infrastructure.

# Customer Migration — Field Notes & Failure Catalog

Real-world failures observed running the lift-and-shift migration against a live
customer server, with the fix for each. **This is the acceptance criteria for the
migration engine**: a customer should be able to migrate, point DNS, and have their
site serve over HTTPS with no server access.

Source of truth for these findings: a real migration on 2026-07-25 from a
HestiaCP/Hostinger box (Debian, nginx 1.25, 72.62.69.9) to a fresh Nxeon VPS
(Ubuntu 22.04, nginx 1.18, 1 vCPU / 2 GB / 25 GB).

---

## The architectural lesson

**Do not blind-copy the source's `/etc/nginx` (or `/etc/apache2`) tree.** That single
behaviour caused roughly half of the failures below. Copying wholesale imports the
source's `nginx.conf`, its include layout, its panel-specific vhosts, its IP
bindings, and its certificate paths — none of which are valid on the target.

Instead:
1. **Parse the source vhosts for intent** — server_name(s), document root or upstream
   proxy target, port, TLS on/off.
2. **Generate clean configs for the target's own web-server version.**
3. Leave the target's `nginx.conf` and include layout **intact**.
4. Copy the source config tree to a reference dir only
   (`/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/source-nginx/`), never into live config.

---

## Failure catalog

### Web server / routing

| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---------|---------|-----|
| 1 | Source `nginx.conf` overwrote the target's | `include sites-enabled/*` disappeared → a generated vhost is **silently ignored** | Write vhosts where the *live* `nginx.conf` actually includes; verify with `nginx -T \| grep <server_name>`, not just `nginx -t` |
| 2 | Hardcoded source IP in ~21 configs | `bind() to <old-ip>:80 failed (99)` — nginx won't start | Rewrite source IP → target IP everywhere, or generate configs without IP binding |
| 3 | `/etc/letsencrypt` not migrated | 5 vhosts referenced missing certs + `options-ssl-nginx.conf` → config test fails → **web server down** | Migrate `/etc/letsencrypt` (certs, renewal conf, accounts) **or** strip TLS blocks and re-issue via certbot after DNS points over. Never leave a config referencing a missing cert |
| 4 | Web-server version mismatch | `http2 on;` (nginx ≥1.25) is an unknown directive on 1.18 | Detect target nginx version; translate/neutralise incompatible directives |
| 5 | Missing log directories | `open() "/var/log/apache2/domains/..." failed` | `mkdir -p` + `touch` every log path a config references before testing |
| 6 | Dead catch-all default server | Copied `listen <ip>:80 default; proxy_pass http://<ip>:8080;` hijacked everything → **502 on all traffic** | Detect copied default/catch-all servers whose upstream is dead; disable them |
| 7 | `listen` specificity beats `server_name` | An IP-bound block (`listen <ip>:80`) wins over generic `listen 80` regardless of server_name — our vhost never selected. **Repeated on 443** → wrong cert → `ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID` | Generated vhosts must bind the target's public IP explicitly on **both** 80 and 443 when copied configs do |
| 8 | Stale nginx PID after config swap | `invalid PID number "" in /var/run/nginx.pid`; `reload` fails | Use `restart` (not `reload`) after replacing nginx.conf; verify `systemctl is-active` |
| 9 | Multi-tenant wildcard subdomains | Tenant subdomains hit no server block → wrong cert | Add `server_name *.<domain>` when the app is multi-tenant (e.g. a `*_BASE_DOMAIN` env var). **A wildcard cert needs DNS-01** — HTTP-01 cannot issue `*.domain` |

### Application startup

| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---------|---------|-----|
| 10 | Docker **images** not migrated | Standalone containers using locally-built images (`app/frontend:latest`, never in a registry) can never start | `docker save \| gzip` on source → stream → `docker load` on target. Prefer `docker pull` for public-registry images |
| 11 | App configured for the **old domain** | `PUBLIC_APP_URL`/`PUBLIC_API_URL` pointed at the old host — and frameworks like Astro/Next **bake the API URL into the static bundle at build time**. Page loads; nothing works | Detect old-hostname references in copied env; offer to rewrite **and rebuild** the affected image. A frontend calling the old server's API is a *silent* failure |
| 12 | Secrets in a non-standard env file | compose had `${VAR}` placeholders but no `.env` — real file was `prod.env` (used via `--env-file`) | Detect the env file the project actually uses; if placeholders would resolve empty, **refuse to start** and name the missing vars |
| 13 | Absolute binary paths differ between hosts | Migrated systemd units called `/usr/local/bin/node` (manual install on source); target has `/usr/bin/node` (apt) → unit crash-looped **880 times** | Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or rewrite the unit to the target's real path |
| 14 | Framework build artifacts don't transfer | Next.js `.next` copied but had no valid production build → `Could not find a production build` | Detect framework apps and run their build on the target (`next build`), or verify `BUILD_ID` exists before enabling the service |
| 15 | MySQL users & grants not migrated | Dump intentionally skips the `mysql` system schema, so **app DB users vanish** → access-denied despite data being present | Enumerate non-system users, `SHOW GRANTS`, replay `CREATE USER`/`GRANT` on the target preserving password hashes. (Postgres `pg_dumpall` already carries roles) |
| 16 | Stack-manager deployments | Apps deployed via Dokploy/Coolify/Portainer keep env/secrets in the manager's **own database**, not on disk (`/data/compose/<id>/`) | Detect the layout and warn explicitly — file copy alone will miss the secrets |

### Storage / capacity

| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---------|---------|-----|
| 17 | `/var/lib/containerd` is a **separate store** from `/var/lib/docker` | Relocated `/var/lib/docker` to the attached volume; root **still** hit 100% — containerd had grown to 9.4 GB | Relocate/bind-mount **both**; add to `/etc/fstab`; verify with `df -h /var/lib/docker /var/lib/containerd` |
| 18 | Build cache is enormous | `docker builder prune -af` reclaimed **7.1 GB** after two builds | Prune after bring-up; retry once after pruning on ENOSPC before failing |
| 19 | Attached block volume unused | A 20 GB volume was attached but unformatted/unmounted while root filled | Detect an attached disk with no FSTYPE/mountpoint; format ext4, mount persistently by UUID, relocate the container stores onto it |
| 20 | Space estimate ignored Docker overhead | Guardrail estimated the ~11 GB file copy; image pulls/builds blew past it → `no space left on device` killed 2 of 3 compose projects | Include source image bytes + 1.5–2× build/ingest headroom; **re-check free space before the image phase**, not only at start |
| 21 | Small targets get starved | On 1 vCPU / 2 GB, a .NET + Astro build starved the box so hard the **QEMU guest agent stopped responding** | Don't assume the guest agent stays reachable during builds; keep the engine's SSH channel authoritative. Warn when target resources are small relative to detected workload |

---

## Verification bar

The final summary must distinguish **"migrated & running (verified)"** from
**"copied — needs a manual step"**, and verification must **HTTP-probe the real
hostname(s)** — not merely check that a port is listening. Never report success when
the site does not actually serve.

Where full automation is genuinely impossible, say so **actionably** — name the file,
the value, and the command:
- wildcard TLS certs (need DNS-01),
- compiled-in API URLs (need a rebuild),
- stack-manager secrets held in the manager's database,
- standalone containers whose images aren't reproducible.

---

## Same-OS question

Matching the source OS removes a real class of problems (web-server/package version
and config-syntax incompatibilities — items 4 and some of 13), and the wizard
recommends it. **It is not a silver bullet**: items 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14,
15, 17–21 are OS-independent migration-completeness issues.

---

## 2026-07-25 — "reported SUCCESS, customer saw a certificate warning and an Apache default page"

A real customer migration completed and reported success. The customer opened their
main site and got a browser certificate warning, clicked through it, and landed on
the **Apache2 Debian Default Page**. Six of their domains were dark. The run log
said `Sites actually serving: 4/4`.

Five separate failures, all now closed in `worker/migrate-real.ts`.

| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix (implemented) |
|---|---------|---------|-------------------|
| 22 | **The success metric could not fail** | Log line 1: `Sites actually serving: 4/4`. Log line 5: `Sites we could not publish automatically — content.revsports.ca, dealerleads.me, new.nexis.revsports.ca, reel.revsports.ca, stg.studionexis.com, studionexis.com`. The denominator was "domains we chose to publish", so it was 100% by construction | Denominator is now every hostname the **source** served, taken from its own live vhost config before we decide what we can publish (`sourceDomains`). The score is `served/total` against that set, the unserved ones are named, and a run with any unserved domain returns `outcome: "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` |
| 23 | **A 200 from the distribution's default page counted as "serving"** | The existing "make a real request to each domain" probe passed for a domain answering 200 with the Apache2 Debian Default Page | The probe now fetches the **body** as well as the status. Apache "It works!" / "Apache2 Debian Default Page" / "Apache2 Ubuntu Default Page" / "Apache HTTP Server Test Page", nginx "Welcome to nginx!", and empty/near-empty 2xx bodies are all **not serving**. Content is only judged on a 2xx (a 301→HTTPS or a 404 legitimately has a tiny body); short JSON/XML bodies are exempt so an API vhost is never called dark |
| 24 | **TLS name mismatch was invisible** | `studionexis.com` was served `nexis.revsports.ca`'s certificate. Every visitor got a full-page security warning before reaching the site — and the probe used `-k`, so it saw only the status code | After each probe the certificate the server actually presents for that name is read with SNI (`openssl s_client -servername`), and its CN/SAN set is matched against the domain (`*.x` covers exactly one label). No coverage ⇒ **not serving**. Skipped when a container owns 443, where the proxy issues its own certificates after DNS moves |
| 25 | **`203/EXEC` — unit enabled with a binary that does not exist here** | `nexis-next.service` had `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node …`; the target has only `/usr/bin/node` (v20, apt). Crash-looped **78 times** and the migration still reported success | **Executable pre-flight before enabling anything.** Every `ExecStart` / `ExecStartPre` / `ExecStartPost` is parsed for its leading absolute executable (handling `-`/`@`/`+`/`!` prefixes, quoted paths, line continuations, `ExecStart=` list resets; PATH-resolved commands ignored). Missing ⇒ symlink to the same basename found via `command -v`, else copy the file from the source, else **do not enable it** and record a blocking entry naming the unit and the path |
| 26 | **"Never built" apps crash-loop silently** | `/opt/nexis` had no `.next` production build, so even with Node fixed the unit exits 1 forever | **Health gate after enabling.** Units settle, then `NRestarts` is sampled twice: `active` + a counter that is not climbing, or it is a blocker with the last journal lines attached. The Next.js `Could not find a production build in the '.next' directory` message is recognised by name and answered with `next build` |
| 27 | **Two web servers, one port 80** | `apache2` was re-enabled from the source's service list while we generated an nginx config. It could not bind 80 and sat `enabled + failed` — quiet until a reboot, where the race decides whether the site or the default page answers | When we generate our own configuration, every other host web server (`apache2`, `httpd`, `caddy`, `lighttpd` — or `nginx` when we chose Apache) is stopped, **disabled and masked**, and the run says so with the `systemctl unmask` command to reverse it. Step 11 also refuses to re-enable a web server from the source's service list when it is not the one we chose |
| 28 | **Ten minutes of silence at 89%** | The progress bar sat frozen while `apt-get install certbot` ran. A wedged migration and a slow one looked identical | The three genuinely long steps — package install, image transfer, certificate issuance — run inside a heartbeat that emits one line every ~45s naming what is still running and for how long |

### The point about #25

**This failure was already in this document.** It is item 13, written up after an
earlier migration where the same `/usr/local/bin/node` mismatch crash-looped a unit
880 times, with the fix spelled out: *"Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or
rewrite the unit to the target's real path."*

It recurred anyway, on a different customer, four months later — because a documented
fix is not a fix. Nothing in the engine read this file. **That is why #25 is now an
executable pre-flight check that runs before every `systemctl enable`, not a
paragraph.** The general rule this establishes: a failure mode that has been observed
twice belongs in code, and a field note describing a fix nobody implemented is worth
approximately nothing.

### Outcome semantics

`runRealMigration` now returns `outcome: "COMPLETED" | "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` plus
`outcomeReasons`, `sourceDomains`, `unservedDomains` and `blockers`. A migration is
`COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` when any domain the source served does not serve here, when
any domain could not be checked, or when any migrated unit is not running.

`Migration.status` in `prisma/schema.prisma` is a plain `String` (not a Prisma enum),
but the only writer is `worker/migrate.ts`, which sets `status: "DONE"`
unconditionally and persists **only** `summary.results` into `Migration.items.results`.
So the outcome is also emitted as the **first entry of `results`** — step
`Migration outcome: COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`, status `failed` — which is what actually
reaches the customer's screen today. Wiring `summary.outcome` through to
`Migration.status` / a dedicated column is a one-line change in `worker/migrate.ts`
that has not been made.

## Server migration — what it is and how a run unfolds

**The flagship.** A customer enters their old server's IP and root password, picks a target Nxeon
VPS, and the platform lifts their entire stack across: files at the same absolute paths, databases
with users and grants, Docker images and containers, systemd units, crontabs, web-server
configuration regenerated for the target, TLS issued, and then a verification gate that HTTP-probes
every hostname the old server actually served before it will call the run a success.

It is 5,351 lines in `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts` and it earned every one of them. The failure
catalogue in `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` has 28 numbered entries, all observed against real
customer servers.

**Two different things share the word "migration."** Do not confuse them:

| | Customer lift-and-shift | Platform self-move |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `worker/migrate-real.ts`, `worker/migrate-detect.ts`, `worker/migrate.ts`, `lib/actions-migrate.ts` | `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `scripts/migrate-export.sh`, `scripts/migrate-repoint-dns.sh` |
| Moves | a customer's stack onto a Nxeon VPS | Nxeon itself onto another box |
| DNS | customer clicks, per hostname, via Cloudflare | registrar API, dry-run by default |

They never call each other.

**The customer screen.**

```

│  Migrate to Nxeon                                                          │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ①Source ── ②Scan ── ③Destination ── ④What to move ── ⑤Review ── ⑥Run      │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ② WHAT WE FOUND ON 72.62.69.9        (read-only scan — nothing was changed)│
│                                                                            │
│  OS          Debian 12  x86_64          ⚠ target is Ubuntu 22.04           │
│                                         Same-OS avoids a class of problems │
```

**The phase machine.** `runRealMigration()` at `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts:3291`. The number in
the left column is the progress percentage reported to the UI.

```

```

**Read-only detection** — `detectSource()` at `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-detect.ts:709`, using one
fixed, input-free POSIX-sh script `SCAN_SCRIPT` (`:465-663`) delivered over stdin. Detected: web roots
and app type (`wp-config.php`/`artisan`/`manage.py`/`package.json`/`composer.json`), home dirs, DB
engines present and listening, DB **variant + version** from the client banner only (`:526`, parsed at
`:682`/`:695`), DB data-dir size, OS and arch (`/etc/os-release` is **grepped, never sourced** —
untrusted input), Docker containers/images/volume sizes, web-server config trees and every
`server_name`/`ServerName`/`ServerAlias`, cron count, TLS cert *directory names only* (never key
material), listening ports with owning process, app dirs from `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, and running
non-distro services.

The security contract is stated at `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-detect.ts:20-41`: read-only, no secret
ever in a command string (DB credentials go via `/dev/stdin`), reject-never-sanitize, everything
bounded.

**Not detected — do not claim otherwise:**

- **No control-panel detection.** There is no HestiaCP / cPanel / Plesk / DirectAdmin / CyberPanel
  probe anywhere, despite HestiaCP being the source box in the field notes. The only traces are a
  comment at `migrate-real.ts:1616` and a `/conf/web/` path-shape heuristic at `:2827`.
- **No mail-stack migration.** No postfix/dovecot/exim handling. `mail` is only a *port label*
  (`migrate-detect.ts:250`).
- **No PHP version detection or install.** `PkgKey` (`migrate-real.ts:555`) has no PHP entry. The
  generated vhost reuses whatever php-fpm socket already exists on the target
  (`ls -1 /run/php/php*-fpm.sock … | head -n1`, `:4477`, wired in at `:1875`). A source on PHP 8.1
  lands on whatever the target happens to have; with no socket, `phpSocket` is `""` and the vhost
  falls back to `try_files … =404` (`:1873`).
- **No source free-space probe.** Sizes are `du` per item; target free space is a separate action,
  `targetDiskFree()` at `lib/actions-migrate.ts:575`.

**Storage pre-flight** — constants at `migrate-real.ts:205-229`: `IMAGE_OVERHEAD_FACTOR = 2`,
`FS_HEADROOM = 2 GiB`, `IMAGE_PHASE_FLOOR = 1.5 GiB`, `MAX_IMAGE_TRANSFER_BYTES = 24 GiB`,
`MAX_SINGLE_IMAGE_BYTES = 12 GiB`. The formula, `:3468-3470`:

```
fileBytes     = items.totalBytes                       ← FILES ONLY
dockerBytes   = imageBytes × IMAGE_OVERHEAD_FACTOR + volumeBytes
requiredBytes = fileBytes + dockerBytes + FS_HEADROOM
```

This is the **only** mid-flight `throw` in the engine (`:3562-3578`), and free space is re-checked
before the image phase (`:4036`) with a per-image budget (`:4049`) — because field-note item 20 was
"space estimate ignored Docker overhead; image pulls blew past it and killed 2 of 3 compose
projects."

The **double-count postmortem** (commit `05e6605`): `selectedMigrationBytes()` in the *wizard*
(`lib/actions-migrate.ts:214`) had also been adding `imageBytes × 2 + headroom`, and the worker added
the same allowance again. A ~12 GB move was reported as needing **83.6 GB** and refused. The contract
is now documented at both ends — `lib/actions-migrate.ts:225-232`: *"this is FILES ONLY … the worker
pre-flight reads it as `fileBytes` and then adds the Docker image allowance + headroom ITSELF."*
`MIGRATION_HEADROOM_BYTES` survives as `void`-ed dead-but-documented reference at `:204`. The earlier
version of this bug went the *other* way ("UI said 11 GB, the engine needed 47.8 GB") and cost the
user ~40 GB of one-way, unrefundable purchased disk. **No test asserts that the wizard and the engine
agree.**

**The source is never mutated.** Verified by inspection of every source-directed command: the
inventory script is read-only and travels over stdin (`ssh … sh -s < file`, `:3357`) so not even a
temp file is written there; `rsyncPull` is pull-only (`:3348`); databases use `SHOW DATABASES` /
`mysqldump` / `pg_dumpall`; images use `docker save`; unit repair is `test -e` plus a single-file
pull. No DNS change, no service stop, no config edit on the source. This is promised to the customer
at `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx:1478-1495` and in every notification.

## Server migration — the verification gate and COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES

**The bug this exists to kill.** From `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:96-113`: a real customer
migration reported success. The customer opened their main site, got a browser certificate warning,
clicked through, and landed on the **Apache2 Debian Default Page**. Six of their domains were dark.
The run log said `Sites actually serving: 4/4`.

The denominator was *"domains we chose to publish"*, so it was **100% by construction**. Five separate
failures, all now closed:

| # | Failure | Fix, and where |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | The success metric could not fail | Denominator is now every hostname the **source** served, read off its own live vhost config *before* we decide what we can publish (`sourceDomains`, `:3421`, `:3437-3451`) |
| 23 | A 200 from the distro default page counted as serving | The probe fetches the **body**; `defaultPageReason` (`:2137`) rejects Apache "It works!"/Debian/Ubuntu default pages, "Welcome to nginx!", and near-empty 2xx bodies (`NEAR_EMPTY_BODY_BYTES = 64`, `:2107`), with JSON/XML exempt so an API vhost is never called dark |
| 24 | TLS name mismatch was invisible (the probe used `-k`) | `servedCertNames` (`:2163`) reads the cert the server *actually presents* via `openssl s_client -servername`, and `certCoversName` (`:2185`) matches CN/SAN with `*.x` covering exactly one label |
| 25 | `203/EXEC` — a unit enabled with a binary that does not exist here | `preflightUnitExecs` (`:2455`) parses every `ExecStart`/`ExecStartPre`/`ExecStartPost` for its leading absolute executable and refuses to enable a unit whose binary is missing |
| 26 | "Never built" apps crash-loop silently | `unitHealthGate` (`:2570`) samples `NRestarts` twice — `active` **and** a counter that is not climbing — or it is a blocker with journal lines attached |
| 27 | Two web servers, one port 80 | `standDownOtherWebServers` (`:2648`) stops, disables and **masks** every other host web server, and prints the `systemctl unmask` command to reverse it |
| 28 | Ten minutes of silence at 89% | `withHeartbeat` (`:485`) wraps the three genuinely long steps and emits a line every ~45s naming what is still running and for how long |

**The probe.**

```
 probeNames = unique([ ...publishedNames, ...sourceDomains ]).slice(0, 24)   :5123
 unprobed   = the overflow beyond 24                    ← reported as NOT CHECKED, :5217
 sourceDomains itself capped at 40                                          :3442

 per name, FOUR checks — all must pass:
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 1  HTTP status      httpProbe  :2057
                     curl -sS -k --max-time 12 --resolve <domain>:<port>:127.0.0.1
                     → real Host header AND real TLS SNI, never leaves the box
                     HTTPS is authoritative when a cert exists            :5147
                     isServing(code)  :2206   →  /^[1-4]\d\d$/
                     i.e. only 000 (nothing answered) or 5xx fails
 2  content          defaultPageReason  :2137 — judged ONLY on a 2xx        :5152
 3  TLS name match   servedCertNames :2163 + certCoversName :2185           :5170
                     runs whenever ANYTHING listens on 443 — including when
                     we hold no cert for that name, because that is exactly
                     when another site's cert gets served
                     skipped when a container owns 443 (proxy issues its own)
 4  probed at all?   a name we never checked counts AGAINST the run
```

**The code that decides the outcome** — `judgeMigrationOutcome()` at
`/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts:2262`, deliberately extracted as a pure function:

```
 scoredAgainst    = sourceDomains.length ? sourceDomains : probeNames        :2265
 unservedDomains  = scoredAgainst.filter(d => !servingSet.has(d))
 failedProbe      = unservedDomains.filter(d =>  probedSet.has(d))
 uncheckedDomains = unservedDomains.filter(d => !probedSet.has(d))
 …
 outcome: outcomeReasons.length ? "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES" : "COMPLETED"      :2305
```

Four independent reason generators: failed probes (`:2278`), unchecked domains (`:2283`), unhealthy
migrated units (`:2288`), and — importantly — **falling back to `probeNames` is itself a reason**
(`:2293`), because that means the source inventory could not be read and the denominator is not
trustworthy.

So `COMPLETED` requires **all four**: every source hostname serving, every one actually checked, every
migrated unit healthy, and the source inventory readable. There is **no percentage threshold** — one
dark domain is enough. The comment at `:2270` states the principle: *"a name we did not get to probe
counts here too — 'we did not check' is not 'it works'."*

**How the three terminal states are produced.**

```
 COMPLETED              judgeMigrationOutcome → no reasons     migrate.ts:412 status "DONE"
 COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES  judgeMigrationOutcome → ≥1 reason      migrate.ts:412
 FAILED                 an EXCEPTION escaped runRealMigration  migrate.ts:544-553
```

`judgeMigrationOutcome` can never return `FAILED`. Every sub-step is best-effort by design
(`migrate-real.ts:43-45`): it logs into `results` and continues. Only fatal setup asserts (`:3293`,
`:3318`, `:3385`) and the storage refusal (`:3574`) throw.

The mapping, `worker/migrate.ts:407-417`:

```
const clean = summary.outcome === "COMPLETED";
status: clean ? "DONE" : "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES",
step:   clean ? "Completed" : "Finished — some sites need attention",
```

And the honest log line that replaced `4/4`, at `migrate-real.ts:5269-5276` — note the denominator is
now *named*:

```
Migrated & running (verified): N. Copied — may need a manual step: M.
Sites actually serving: X/Y of the domains the old server served.
NOT serving on the new server: a.com, b.com — do not move DNS for these names yet.
```

The "could not publish automatically" list is still emitted (`:4552`) but those names are now **also
pushed into `blockers`** (`:4558`), with the comment: *"These are BLOCKING, not a footnote. On
2026-07-25 this exact line named six domains while the headline said 4/4 serving."*

**The UI honours it.** `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx:1318` lists the terminal states,
`:1335` computes `withIssues`, and `:1396-1408` renders an **amber** card, not the emerald "Migration
complete 🎉". The comment at `:1390` records why: showing the green card for
`COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` is what let a customer walk away believing they were live.

**Rollback is deliberately not offered.** `MigrationWizard.tsx:1491-1495`: no action against the old
server and no undo on the new one, *"so the cutover can be retried the moment the problem is fixed — a
rollback that destroyed the migrated copy would turn one bad afternoon into a repeat of the whole
transfer."* Rollback means pointing the A record back, and the DNS card renders for **every** terminal
state including `FAILED` (`:1429`).

Partial-target cleanup is narrow and safety-directed: only broken web config is reverted — a rejected
nginx conf is removed and nginx restarted (`:4653`), a rejected Apache vhost is `a2dissite`'d
(`:4698`) — under the invariant at `:4654`, *"NEVER leave the web server unable to start."* Pre-change
snapshots are kept at `${work}/nginx-before` and `${work}/apache-before`. Migrated files, databases,
images and containers are left in place.

Secret scrubbing always runs (`finally`, `:5318`): `shred -u` on the SSH pass file, per-container env
files, the MySQL grants SQL (password hashes), and the Cloudflare DNS-01 ini. **DB dumps under
`${work}/dumps` are intentionally kept** (`:5324`) so a failed import can be retried by hand, and the
customer is told so.

**Honest notes on the gate.**

- **`test/migration-gate.test.ts` does not exist.** `migrate-real.ts:2217` says the scoring rule *"is
  exercised by `test/migration-gate.test.ts` instead of only ever being exercised by a real
  customer's cutover."* `test/` holds `billing-terms`, `games`, `growth`, `rate-limit`, `totp` and
  nothing else. The most safety-critical function in the subsystem is untested, in a comment claiming
  it is tested. This is the recurring defect in its purest form: a *verification claim* that was
  never verified.
- **`docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:136-143` is stale.** It says `worker/migrate.ts` "sets
  `status: "DONE"` unconditionally" and that wiring the outcome through is "a one-line change that has
  not been made." It **has** been made (`worker/migrate.ts:412`). The same stale claim is repeated
  inside the engine at `migrate-real.ts:5251`. That document's own thesis is that unread field notes
  are worthless; this is the mirror case — a fixed note nobody updated.
- **`prisma/schema.prisma:1009` lists four statuses; the code writes five.** The comment says
  `PENDING | RUNNING | DONE | FAILED`; `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` is missing from it.
- **There is no rehearsal harness.** No migration test exists. Every bug so far was found by a real
  migration onto a real customer domain. The next customer migration is the gate's first real test.

## Server migration — cutover, re-runs and the missing TLS retry

**DNS repointing is manual, customer-initiated, one click per hostname.** The engine never touches
DNS.

```
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  Point your domains at the new server                               │
 ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │  studionexis.com        registered with Nxeon    → 51.79.162.96     │
 │                                                     [ Point now ]   │
 │  content.example.ca     found on the new server     [ Point now ]   │
 │  stg.example.com        from the old server's vhosts  ✗ NOT SERVING │
 │                         do not move DNS for this name yet           │
 │                                                                     │
 │  Or roll back: point the A record at your old server.               │
 │  [ Open Cloudflare DNS ↗ ]                                          │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Candidates come from three sources — `getMigrationDnsInfo()` at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-migrate.ts:743`:
`Domain` rows registered with Nxeon (`:764`), `Website` rows on the target (`:772`), and hostnames
inferred from the **stored** scan snapshot's web-root folder names (`:779`). It explicitly never
re-scans the source (`:741`).

The write is `pointMigrationDns()` at `:804` → `pointHostnameToIp` (`lib/cloudflare-point.ts:97`).
Cloudflare only. A **single DNS-only A record**, `proxied: false` — which is load-bearing: an orange-
clouded record breaks HTTP-01 validation, and HTTP-01 is the only challenge the SSL subsystem uses
(`lib/cloudflare-point.ts:12-17`, `:158-162`).

**Cloudflare is involved three ways:** the A-record write above; **DNS-01 wildcard issuance** — a
`*.domain` certificate cannot be issued any other way, so `resolveTlsInputs()`
(`worker/migrate.ts:186`) resolves the customer's token and passes it as `cloudflareToken` (`:389`) to
`secureSites` rung 3 (`migrate-real.ts:3125`) → `issueDns01` (`:2991`); and a deep link for manual
rollback (`MigrationWizard.tsx:1596`).

**How an admin re-runs a failed migration: there is no re-run path.** Verified:

- No admin UI. `db.migration` is referenced only in `lib/actions-migrate.ts`; there is no
  `app/admin/**` migration page at all.
- No retry action. The exported actions are `createMigration` (`:324`), `scanSource` (`:461`),
  `targetDiskFree` (`:575`), `listMigrations` (`:675`), `getMigration` (`:694`),
  `getMigrationDnsInfo` (`:743`), `pointMigrationDns` (`:804`). None re-enqueues.
- No CLI. `scripts/migrate-*.sh` are for moving the platform, not a customer.
- The worker will not retry either: the handler swallows the error (`worker/migrate.ts:562`), so the
  `Job` completes and `MAX_ATTEMPTS` never engages.
- **The secrets are already gone.** `clearSecrets` runs on failure (`migrate.ts:555`), so a bare
  re-enqueue of the same `migrationId` fails at `migrate-real.ts:3318` with *"source SSH password is
  missing or could not be decrypted."*

**The only supported route is to start a new migration** — `MigrationWizard.tsx:1436` ("← Start
another migration") → `createMigration` with freshly entered credentials, rate-limited to 5 per 10
minutes (`lib/actions-migrate.ts:331`). Re-runs are safe by construction: user/group creation
(`:3721`), volume create (`:3781`), `ensureImage`'s present-check (`:1417`) and the
Docker-already-on-its-own-FS pre-flight allowance (`:3472`) are all idempotent.

**The one thing you *can* re-enqueue by hand** is the TLS pass:

```
db.job.create({ data: { type: "MIGRATE", payload: { migrationId, phase: "tls" } } })
```

Documented at `worker/migrate.ts:257`, idempotent via certbot `--keep-until-expiring` (`:251`), copies
nothing (`:245`), and deliberately does **not** touch `Migration.status` (`:252`).

**Honest note — the post-cutover TLS retry has zero callers.** `runPostCutoverTls`
(`worker/migrate.ts:260`) is reached only when `payload.phase === "tls"` (`:341`), and the enqueue
line exists **only inside a comment** (`:258`). A repo-wide grep for `phase: "tls"` returns that
comment and nothing else. `pointMigrationDns` does not enqueue it. So certificates that could not be
issued at migration time — because DNS had not moved yet, which is the normal case — are **never
retried automatically**. `issueMigrationCertificates` (`migrate-real.ts:3236`) exists precisely to

**1. There is no UI to save a card, so renewal auto-charge can never fire.** *DEAD.*
The engine is real and wired (`worker/billing.ts:28-43` imports 13 symbols from `lib/stripe-cards`),
but `lib/actions-payment-method.ts` — `startCardSetup` `:46`, `finalizeCardSetup` `:72`,
`removeSavedCard` `:101`, `settleOutstanding` `:127` — has **zero callers** in `app/` or
`components/`. Every renewal is therefore wallet-only, and a customer with an empty wallet goes
straight to grace → suspend: precisely the outcome the dunning engine was built to prevent. This is
the single highest-value wiring job outstanding.

**2. The hardened firewall is in the file, not in the kernel.** *NOT APPLIED.*
`scripts/firewall.nft` has been rewritten to restrict the two administrative ports —
`define ADMIN_PORTS = { 22, 8006 }` (`:120`), accepted only from `@nxeon_admin_v4`/`@nxeon_admin_v6`
(`:190-191`) — and the comment at `:21-35` explains why: a successful login on `:8006` is
*"not 'a server gets hacked', it is 'the hosting company ends'"*. But the **live** ruleset still reads:

```
tcp dport { 22, 80, 443, 8006, 8080, 8443 } accept
```

So Proxmox's web UI and host SSH are reachable from the internet right now. Populate the admin sets and
apply with `scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh` (it has a rollback timer — do not `nft -f` by hand over an
SSH session you cannot afford to lose).

**3. Game auto-update cannot fail.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS — runs unattended every 6 hours.*
`worker/game-update.ts:60` returns `set -e; ${steam}${restart}; true`. steamcmd is `|| true` (`:51`)
and skipped entirely when absent; every restart branch is `|| true` (`:59`); the command ends `; true`.
The remote command **cannot** exit non-zero, so `:134` always fires *"The latest server update was
applied and the service was restarted."* `worker/apps.ts` is now the model for how to fix this — it
proves the outcome with `verifyServing()` and fails the job with the real HTTP result.

**4. Post-cutover TLS is never retried.** *DEAD.* `runPostCutoverTls` (`worker/migrate.ts:260`) is
reached only via `payload.phase === "tls"`, and the enqueue line exists **only inside a comment**
(`:258`) — a repo-wide grep for `phase: "tls"` returns that comment and nothing else.
`pointMigrationDns` does not trigger it. So names that could not be issued at migration time — the
normal case, since DNS has not moved yet — are never retried.
`issueMigrationCertificates` (`migrate-real.ts:3236`) exists for exactly this and still effectively has
no caller. Until it is wired, closing the loop means queueing the job by hand (see the migration
re-run runbook).

**5. Migration simulation still reports success when the flag is off.** *SIMULATED — dormant.*
Unlike SSL and game-config, which now throw, `worker/migrate.ts:452` falls through to a synthetic
branch that fabricates step results, writes `status: "DONE"` / `step: "Completed"` (`:533`) and
notifies *"Migration to X completed"* (`:536`). Its sleep timings were written for the non-sandbox
case. `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION=1` today, so it is dormant — **one lost `.env` line re-creates the
original lie on the flagship feature.** The same fall-through shape applies to the four
`ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` workers (`websites.ts:39`, `apps.ts:81`, `databases.ts:35`, `services.ts:34`).

**6. Nxeon-registered domains get no mail DNS.** *PARTIAL — the UI promises otherwise.*
`components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:261` tells the customer that a domain registered with Nxeon has
*"its mail DNS managed for you — mailboxes go live automatically."* Nothing publishes
MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC at name.com: `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:283` only ever adds A records. Their mail
will not work, and the panel says it will.

**7. `email_mx_host` and `email_spf_include` change nothing.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD — and the panel makes
an explicit false claim about its own effect.* `components/admin/settings/GeneralPanel.tsx:26` says
*"Shown in the customer business-email DNS setup panel"*; `:34` says *"Rendered as
`v=spf1 include:<value> ~all`"*. Neither is true. The real values are hardcoded at
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:36` (`mail.nxeon.cloud`) and `:41` (`nxeon.cloud`), while the admin
fields default to `mx.nxeon.email` and `_spf.nxeon.email` — so the panel makes correctly-configured
mail look misconfigured, and editing either field does nothing.

**8. Domain-ownership verification uses the wrong resolver.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:5` imports the top-level `resolveTxt`/`resolveMx`, used at `:464` and
`:474` — so verification runs against `/etc/resolv.conf` (OVH's cache), not the zone's authority. A
customer who has just published `_nxeon-verify` can be told it is not there.
`lib/mail/deliverability.ts` does it correctly and is the model to copy. The same bug is in
`app/api/tools/dns/route.ts:35` (a `Resolver` with no `setServers`) and
`app/api/tools/my-ip/route.ts:23` (`reverse` on the default resolver).

**9. There is no PTR / reverse-DNS check anywhere.** *Missing.* `checkDeliverability` covers only
`mx | spf | dkim | dmarc` (`lib/mail/deliverability.ts:41`) — despite the motivating incident being a
*reverse* lookup. And the correct checker `checkEmailDeliverability`
(`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:523`) has **no caller**, so there is no UI entry point at all.
`components/admin/MailAnalytics.tsx:135-148`'s "DNS & DMARC" card is static prose, not a check.

**10. Cloudflare connections cannot refresh.** *PARTIAL.* The working scope in `.env:39` omits
`offline_access`, so Cloudflare issues no refresh token and every connection dies at `expiresAt`
(`lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:332` → `CF_RECONNECT`) with no re-auth prompt. Separately the **code
default** scope (`:59`) is a value Cloudflare rejects, so any deploy that loses that env var
reintroduces the "invalid scope" error a customer hit three times.

# Migration rehearsal — first real end-to-end run of the verification gate

**Date:** 2026-07-26 · **Engine:** `worker/migrate-real.ts` (5,351 lines, unmodified)
**Verdict on the headline question:** the gate's *scoring logic* is correct and it did
**not** report success while a site was dark. But it is being fed **corrupted inputs**,
and it **measures only two of the many things a migration can lose**. Both are detailed
below with reproductions.

This is the first time the gate has run against a real migration. Every defect below was
found in a single 3-minute run.

---

## 1. What was rehearsed

Two throwaway VMs on this host, matching the OS pair from the field notes
(Debian 12 → Ubuntu 22.04):

| | vmid | OS | IP |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source | 9500 `rehearsal-src-deb12` | Debian GNU/Linux 12 | 10.20.0.150 |
| Target | 9501 `rehearsal-dst-ubuntu2204` | Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS | 10.20.0.151 |

The source was built to be deliberately messy, one item per failure class:

- **nginx, 3 vhosts on FQDNs** — `shop.rehearsal-src.example.com` (301→HTTPS, self-signed
  cert in `/etc/letsencrypt/live/`), `blog.othertenant.example.net` (HTTP only, **no cert
  of its own** — the field-note 24 shape), `legacy.defaultpage.example.org`
  (docroot `/var/www/html`).
- **`/var/www/html/index.html` = the Apache2 Debian Default Page** (field note 23).
- **MariaDB 10.11** with `shopdb` (5 orders + 3 products) and two application accounts
  with grants — `shopapp@localhost`, `readonly@%` (field note 15).
- **A systemd unit whose `ExecStart`/`ExecStartPre` point at `/usr/local/bin/node`**, a
  hand-installed Node **v20.11.1** that does not exist on the target (field notes 13 & 25).
- **A Docker Compose project** at `/opt/stack` (redis + nginx, published on 6399/8099).
- Crontabs, `/etc/cron.d`, and a compose env var pointing at the old hostname.

Reserved TLDs (`example.com/.net/.org`) were used throughout so no real domain could be
touched. `resolvesHere()` gates HTTP-01 on the name already resolving to the target, so
**no Let's Encrypt traffic was generated**; no Cloudflare token was passed, so no DNS-01.

### How the engine was driven

`worker/migrate-real.ts` contains **zero `db.` references** — the engine takes plain
objects. It was therefore driven directly with a synthetic `migration` + `target`, so the
rehearsal wrote **nothing** to the platform database: no `Migration` row, no `Job`, no
`Server`, no customer row touched. The real `detectSource()` ran first, and `items` was
built by replicating `createMigration`'s `derivePlan` / `selectedMigrationBytes`
(`lib/actions-migrate.ts:135`, `:214`) exactly.

Run time: **3.0 minutes**. Result: `outcome: "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"`,
`Sites actually serving: 1/4`.

---

## 2. Did the gate report the truth?

**On domains: yes.** It correctly refused to call the run a success, named all three
unserved hostnames, and told the customer not to move DNS for them. The `4/4`-style lie
from 2026-07-25 did **not** reproduce.

**But the honesty is narrower than it looks, in three distinct ways:**

1. **`judgeMigrationOutcome` only sees domains and systemd units.** Its inputs are
   `{ sourceDomains, probeNames, siteProbes, unitBlockers }` (`migrate-real.ts:5248`).
   A step result with `status: "failed"` does **not** affect the outcome. In this very run
   `Migrate database users` was pushed as **`failed`** and the outcome reasons never
   mentioned it. A migration that loses every database account, every cron job, every
   standalone container and a whole selected directory tree can still return
   **`COMPLETED`**, provided the web pages happen to answer. See defects 1b, 6, 7.
2. **Two of its four inputs are corrupted before it sees them** (defects 1a, 2). The
   scorer is provably correct — 32/32 tests pass — and still produces a wrong answer,
   because `unitBlockers` contains a healthy service and `sourceDomains` contains a
   hostname the source never served.
3. **It cries wolf on every run.** Because of defects 1a and 2, `COMPLETED` is
   effectively unreachable on any Debian/Ubuntu source that runs any systemd service —
   i.e. essentially all of them. A gate that always says `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` trains
   the reader to skim it, which is how a genuinely dark domain ships.

**The structural reason the tests missed all of this:** `test/migration-gate.test.ts`
(32 tests, all passing) covers exactly the functions that were *extracted for
testability* — `defaultPageReason`, `isServing`, `certCoversName`, `parseUnitExecPaths`,
`preflightUnitExecs`, `judgeMigrationOutcome`. Every bug below lives in the **unextracted
SSH glue that builds those functions' arguments**. The pure core is correct; the
plumbing into it is not.

---

## 3. Defects

### 1. `clean()` destroys the row structure of every multi-row command output — systemic

`clean()` at **`worker/migrate-real.ts:356`**:

```ts
return String(s ?? "").replace(/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/g, "").trim().slice(0, max);
```

`\x0a` (newline) and `\x09` (tab) are both inside `\x00-\x1f`, so **every newline and tab
is deleted**. It is then used on multi-row output that is immediately `.split("\n")`-ed or
tab-parsed. The split yields **one element containing everything concatenated**.

The codebase already knows this hazard — `probeBody` (`:2094`) exists solely to avoid it
and its docblock says *"Deliberately NOT `clean()`: `clean` strips ALL control characters
including newlines, which would glue … and make the markers unmatchable."* That lesson was
applied to the probe body and to nowhere else.

**Reproduction** (`node`, replicating `clean` verbatim):

```
$ node -e '
const clean=(s,max)=>String(s??"").replace(/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/g,"").trim().slice(0,max);
console.log(JSON.stringify(clean("NRestarts=0\nActiveState=active\nSubState=running\n",512)));'
"NRestarts=0ActiveState=activeSubState=running"
```

Confirmed call sites, each independently broken:

#### 1a. The unit health gate can never report a healthy unit — `:2537-2538`

```ts
const out = clean(r.stdout, 512);
const pick = (k) => new RegExp(`${k}=([A-Za-z0-9-]*)`).exec(out)?.[1] ?? "";
```

`systemctl show` returns (verified on the target, in this order):

```
NRestarts=0
ActiveState=active
SubState=running
```

After `clean()` → `NRestarts=0ActiveState=activeSubState=running`, so:

| pick | returns | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `ActiveState` | **`"activeSubState"`** | `b.active === "active"` is **never true** → `ok` is always false → **every migrated unit becomes a blocker** |
| `SubState` | `"running"` | — |
| `NRestarts` | **`"0ActiveState"`** → `Number(...)` = **`NaN`** → coerced to `0` | `climbing = b.restarts > a.restarts` is **always false** → **the crash-loop detector of field note 26 can never fire** |

**Observed in the run** — a unit that is genuinely `active/running` with `NRestarts=0`:

```
legacyapp: NOT running — it never became active (systemd reports activeSubState/running).
  Its last log lines were: … | legacyapp listening on 3105
```

That corrupted `activeSubState/running` string is the fingerprint. Ground truth on the
target immediately afterwards:

```
$ systemctl is-active legacyapp   → active
$ systemctl show legacyapp -p NRestarts --value → 0
$ curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3105/  → 200
```

The journal lines quoted **in the blocker itself** say `legacyapp listening on 3105`. The
engine attached proof of health to a report of failure.

Severity: this is the field-note-26 mechanism inverted. It cannot confirm health, and it
cannot detect a crash loop — a unit restarting 78 times is reported with the wrong reason
("never became active") purely by accident.

#### 1b. Database-user migration always reports total failure — `:3908-3913`

```ts
const present = new Set(
  clean(check.stdout, 8000).split("\n").map((l) => l.split(/\s+/).slice(0, 2).join("@"))
);
```

`mysql -N -B -e "SELECT user, host FROM mysql.user"` is tab-separated and multi-row.
`clean()` removes **both** separators, so `present` is a single garbage string and
`landed` is **always empty** → the `else` branch at `:3937` always runs.

**Observed:** `[failed] Migrate database users :: none of the 3 application database
account(s) could be recreated — apps that log in as their own DB user will get
access-denied until they are created by hand`

**Ground truth — the grants replayed perfectly, hashes and all:**

```
$ mysql -u shopapp -pShopAppRehearsalPw1 -N -e 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shopdb.orders;'
5
$ mysql -N -e 'SHOW GRANTS FOR "shopapp"@"localhost";'
GRANT USAGE ON *.* TO `shopapp`@`localhost` IDENTIFIED BY PASSWORD '*AD13F7F645CB…'
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON `shopdb`.* TO `shopapp`@`localhost`
```

Field note 15's fix **works**; its verification lies about it. The customer is told to
hand-recreate accounts that already exist and function — and the note is `failed`, the
loudest status the summary has.

Reproduction: `Set(clean("readonly\t%\nshopapp\tlocalhost\n",8000).split("\n").map(l=>l.split(/\s+/).slice(0,2).join("@")))`
→ `{'readonly%shopapplocalhost'}`.

#### 1c. The stale-reference sweep silently finds nothing, ever — `:4935`

```ts
for (const raw of clean(out.stdout, 60000).split("\n")) {
  const tab = raw.indexOf("\t");
  if (tab < 0) continue;          // ← always taken
```

`clean()` strips tabs unconditionally, so `indexOf("\t")` is **always `-1`** and **every
line is skipped**. This is not order-dependent — it fails 100% of the time.

**Observed:** the run logged *"Scanning the copied files for anything still pointing at the
old server"* and then put **`Old-server references`** into `verifiedRunning` — a clean
bill of health produced by parsing zero lines.

This is the detection for **field note 11** (*"App configured for the old domain … A
frontend calling the old server's API is a silent failure"*). It is dead, and it reports
success.

#### 1d. Compose env-file discovery is dead — `:4358`, `:4365`, `:4370`, `:4379`

```ts
envFiles = clean(find.stdout, 8000).split("\n").map(s=>s.trim()).filter(p=>validPath(p))
```

Three found files collapse into one impossible path
(`/opt/stack/.env/opt/stack/prod.env/var/www/app/.env`). Whether it survives `validPath`
or not, the real files are never examined. This kills:

- **field note 12** — the `prod.env` / missing-`.env` placeholder detection that is
  supposed to *refuse to start* and name the missing vars;
- **field note 11**'s old-hostname scan of env files (`staleEnvFiles`, `staleVars`);
- **field note 9** — `baseDomain` (`:4379`) is how a multi-tenant wildcard `server_name`
  is detected, so `*.domain` vhosts are never generated.

#### 1e. `resolvesHere()` fails for any domain with more than one A record — `:2931-2932`

```ts
const r = await sh(conn, `getent ahostsv4 ${domain} … | sort -u | head -n 8`);
return clean(r.stdout, 512).split("\n").map(s=>s.trim()).includes(ip);
```

`sort -u` collapses a single-IP answer to one line, which is why this works in the common
case. A round-robin / multi-A hostname returns 2+ lines → concatenated → `includes(ip)`
is **false** → the name is declared "does not point at the new server yet" → **HTTP-01 is
skipped and no certificate is ever issued**, even after the customer has correctly moved
DNS. Combined with "post-cutover TLS is never retried" (Known gaps 4) that domain never
gets a certificate at all.

```
$ node -e 'const c=(s,m)=>String(s).replace(/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/g,"").trim().slice(0,m);
for(const o of ["10.20.0.151\n","10.20.0.151\n10.20.0.152\n"])
console.log(JSON.stringify(o), c(o,512).split("\n").map(s=>s.trim()).includes("10.20.0.151"));'
"10.20.0.151\n" true
"10.20.0.151\n10.20.0.152\n" false
```

#### 1f. Same pattern, lower impact

`:1368` (df tail, cosmetic — re-joined anyway), `:4145` (docker volume verification
tokens), `:4425` (step-10 parse).

---

### 2. Phantom hostnames from **commented-out** config poison the denominator

`migrate-real.ts:910` harvests server names with:

```
grep -rhoE 'server_name[[:space:]]+[^;]+' /etc/nginx
```

There is no comment filter, and the parse at `:1069-1076` only strips the directive
keyword. Debian's and Ubuntu's **stock** `/etc/nginx/sites-available/default` ships:

```
/etc/nginx/sites-available/default:83:#	server_name example.com;
```

**Observed:** `example.com` entered `sourceDomains` — *the denominator* — was probed,
could not serve (nothing was ever generated for it), and became one of the three
outcome-driving failures:

```
sourceDomains (DEN): ["blog.othertenant.example.net","shop.rehearsal-src.example.com",
                      "example.com","legacy.defaultpage.example.org"]
Sites actually serving: 1/4 of the domains the old server served.
```

The honest denominator was **3**. The score `1/4` is wrong, `example.com` is named to the
customer as a site they must fix, and it consumes probe budget (capped at 24, `:5127`).

Because that file ships enabled-or-not on virtually every Debian/Ubuntu box, **almost
every real migration inherits a permanent phantom failure**, so `COMPLETED` becomes
unreachable. Field note 22 replaced a denominator that could not fail with one that
cannot succeed.

Reproduction: `grep -rhoE 'server_name[[:space:]]+[^;]+' /etc/nginx` on any stock
Debian 12 box with nginx installed.

---

### 3. `COMPLETED` is unreachable in practice

Defects 1a and 2 compose. Any source with ≥1 migrated systemd unit gets a permanent
`unitBlockers` entry; any Debian/Ubuntu source gets a permanent phantom domain. Together
they guarantee `outcomeReasons.length > 0` at `:2305`. The state the UI renders emerald
for (`MigrationWizard.tsx:1396`) is dead code in the field.

---

### 4. The gate's own advice deadlocks on certless vhosts

For `blog.othertenant.example.net` the single run emitted both:

```
[copied] HTTPS for blog… :: this name does not point at the new server yet (10.20.0.151),
         and a certificate cannot be issued until DNS moves. To finish: point the DNS, then
         run: certbot certonly --webroot …
[report] NOT serving on the new server: blog…, example.com, legacy… — do not move DNS for
         these names yet.
```

*Point the DNS to get a certificate* and *do not point the DNS* — in the same summary,
about the same hostname. The cert-mismatch verdict (defect 5) can only be cleared by
moving DNS, which the summary forbids. A customer following the instructions cannot
finish. `migrate-real.ts:5262` (the "do not move DNS" line) needs to distinguish
"broken here" from "waiting on your DNS".

---

### 5. Cert-mismatch marks HTTP-only sites dark, though they serve exactly as before

Check (ii) at `:5169-5185` runs *whenever anything is listening on 443*, including for
names we hold no certificate for — deliberately, per the comment. Consequence:

- `blog.othertenant.example.net` was **HTTP-only on the source** and serves byte-identical
  content on the target (`curl` → `200`, real body verified).
- On the target only `shop`'s certificate exists, so it answers 443 as the default server.
- Verdict: **NOT serving**, *"every visitor gets a full-page browser security warning"*.

The source behaved the same way — `openssl s_client -servername blog… ` on the **source**
also returns `subject=CN = shop.rehearsal-src.example.com`. So the migration is penalised
for a pre-existing condition it faithfully reproduced, on a site that works.

On any box where some vhosts have certificates and others do not — the normal HestiaCP/
cPanel shape — **every certless vhost is declared dark.** The verdict should distinguish
"the source served this over HTTPS and we broke it" (a real regression, and the actual
`studionexis.com` incident) from "this was always plain HTTP".

Note also the message is misleading: for these names the *authoritative* probe was HTTP
(`httpsRes` is empty, `:5148`), yet the reason says *"this server answers
https://blog…/ with a certificate issued for …"*.

---

### 6. Every standalone container is invisible — the primary `docker inspect` template always fails

`migrate-real.ts:864` in the inventory script:

```
"devices {{len .HostConfig.Devices}}",
```

Running **the engine's own generated script** (recovered from
`/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/src-1.sh`) against the source, with the `2>/dev/null` at
`:886` removed:

```
template parsing error: template: :9:10: executing "" at <len .HostConfig.Devices>:
  error calling len: len of nil pointer
```

— once per container, for **both** containers, Docker 29.6.2. The whole template aborts,
so the primary inspect emits **nothing**. Only the *second* inspect (`IFMT`, image
cmd/entrypoint) survives, which is why the parsed containers carry no `name` and no
`image` and are dropped by the filter at `:1123`:

```
$ cut -f1 inv.out | sort | uniq -c        # engine's own script output
      4 C          ← only imagecmd / imageentrypoint
      2 IMAGE
      1 INVENTORY_OK
$ grep '^C' inv.out
C	d60e8dae1e41	imagecmd nginx~-g~daemon off;~
C	d60e8dae1e41	imageentrypoint /docker-entrypoint.sh~
```

**Observed:** `Found 2 image(s) (151 MB), 0 container(s), …` — while the read-only scan
(`migrate-detect.ts`, which does not use this template) correctly reported
`containers: ["rehearsal-api","rehearsal-cache"]`.

The nil-safe form works: `{{if .HostConfig.Devices}}{{len .HostConfig.Devices}}{{else}}0{{end}}`.

**Why this is the most dangerous defect found.** `inv.containers` is empty ⇒

- `standalone = srcContainers.filter(c => !c.project)` (`:4222`) is empty, so **step 9c
  recreates nothing**;
- the "we could not re-read its settings" fallback at `:4223` is guarded on
  **`!inv.probed`**, which is **true here** (`INVENTORY_OK` was emitted — only the
  container inspect failed), so that branch is skipped too;
- ⇒ a customer's standalone containers are **silently not recreated and never mentioned**;
- `appPorts` (`:4486`) is also always empty, so the container-port fallback for generating
  a vhost upstream never has a port to use.

This is the failure mode the owner asked about, in its purest form: **a non-HTTP
standalone container (a queue worker, a cron sidecar) is lost, nothing in the summary
mentions it, and because the score only counts domains and units, the outcome can still be
`COMPLETED`.** The field-note customer box had 15 containers; all 15 would have been
invisible.

---

### 7. Paths filtered by `safeCopyTarget` are dropped with no report line

`migrate-real.ts:3306`:

```ts
const paths = rawPaths.filter(safeCopyTarget);
```

`UNSAFE_EXACT` (`:327`) contains **`/home`**. There is no log line, no `results` entry and
no `needsAttention` entry for the difference between `rawPaths` and `paths`.

**Observed:** 4 paths selected (`/var/www`, `/home`, `/opt/legacyapp`, `/opt/stack`), and
the engine reported `Copying 3 path(s)` / `Copy 3 folder(s) to their original paths`. The
customer is told 3 and never told which one vanished or why.

This is reachable from the wizard's own defaults: `DEFAULT_PATHS = ["/var/www", "/home"]`
(`lib/actions-migrate.ts:110`) is substituted by `cleanPaths` whenever the customer
selects no paths — so the default selection contains a path the engine silently discards.
For a control-panel source where sites live under `/home/<user>/public_html` (the
HestiaCP layout in the field notes) that is the entire web estate.

`assert(paths.length || …)` at `:3309` still passes because `/var/www` survived, so there
is no error either.

---

### 8. Distro units are reported as customer action items

Seven entries in `needsAttention` (of 22 total) read:

```
Service containerd — unit not a simple /etc/systemd/system file — re-enable manually
Service docker    — …
Service exim4     — …
Service mariadb   — …
Service nginx     — …
Service qemu-guest-agent — …
Service serial-getty@ttyS0 — …
```

These are distro-packaged units the target already has and already runs — `nginx` and
`mariadb` were installed *by this migration* and are active. Telling the customer to
re-enable `nginx` manually, in the same run that says `nginx restarted`, is noise that
dilutes the two entries that matter. Note this also contradicts field note 27's rule
about not re-enabling a web server from the source's service list.

### 9. `verifyPorts` carries source-OS noise into a failure line

`derivePlan` takes every listening port (`lib/actions-migrate.ts:165`), so `25` (exim4)
and `5355` (systemd-resolved mDNS) were verified on the target and reported as
`Ports not yet listening — not up on the target yet: 25, 5355 — start the owning
app/service`. Neither is the customer's application.

### 10. The exec pre-flight bridges incompatible major versions and calls them the same program

The symlink repair at `:2489-2497` matched on **basename only**:

```
legacyapp: /usr/local/bin/node does not exist here, so it was linked to /usr/bin/node
           (the same program, installed in a different place).
```

Ground truth:

```
source /usr/local/bin/node → v20.11.1
target /usr/bin/node       → v12.22.9      (Ubuntu 22.04 apt; EOL since 2022)
```

Eight major versions apart, and the older one is end-of-life. The claim *"the same
program"* is false. My trivial app survived; a Next.js or Vite app will not start on
Node 12, and field note 14 ("framework build artifacts don't transfer") lands right on top
of this. The repair is the correct strategy but should compare `--version` between source
and target and record the jump as a blocker or at least a warning.

### 11. Two stale in-code claims

- **`migrate-real.ts:5251-5253`** still says *"worker/migrate.ts writes Migration.status =
  "DONE" unconditionally and persists ONLY summary.results"*. It has not done that since
  `migrate.ts:407-417`. Already flagged in `DOCUMENTATION.md`; still present.
- **`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` "Known gaps"** claims *"`test/migration-gate.test.ts` does not
  exist"* and that the scoring rule is untested. **It exists and passes 32/32.** The
  document is now wrong in the reassuring direction — the opposite of the error it was
  written to catch. What is true is that the tests cover only the extracted pure
  functions, which is why they caught none of the defects above.

The rehearsal is complete, VMs destroyed, findings written to `/opt/nxeon/docs/MIGRATION-REHEARSAL.md`.

## Answer to your central question

**The gate did not report success while a site was dark** — that specific failure mode did not reproduce. It returned `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`, scored `1/4` against the source's own vhosts, and named every unserved hostname. Default-page detection and cert-mismatch detection **both fired correctly** on exactly the shapes from the 2026-07-25 incident, and the `ExecStart` pre-flight **resolved** the bad unit before enabling it — field note 13 did not recur.

But the honesty is narrower than it looks, in a way that matters:

**`judgeMigrationOutcome` only measures domains and systemd units.** A step result with `status: "failed"` does not affect the outcome at all. In this run `Migrate database users` was pushed as `failed` and the outcome reasons never mentioned it. Anything that isn't an HTTP-serving hostname — containers, cron, DB accounts, dropped paths — can go missing and still yield `COMPLETED`.

## The 11 defects, headline three

1. **`clean()` (`migrate-real.ts:356`) deletes newlines *and tabs*, then its output is `.split("\n")`-ed in six verification paths.** The codebase already documented this hazard for `probeBody` and applied the lesson nowhere else. Confirmed empirically: a perfectly healthy unit was reported `NOT running — systemd reports activeSubState/running` (that corrupted string is the fingerprint; `NRestarts` parses to `NaN`, so **field note 26's crash-loop detector can never fire**). Same bug reports "none of the 3 DB accounts could be recreated" when all had landed with hashes and grants intact, and makes the stale-reference sweep parse **zero lines while reporting success**. Field notes 9, 11, 12 and 26 are all inert in production.

2. **`devices {{len .HostConfig.Devices}}` (`:864`) aborts the whole Go template on nil.** Every container is invisible (`0 container(s)` while the read-only scan found 2), so step 9c recreates nothing — and the "couldn't re-read settings" fallback is guarded on `!inv.probed`, which is false here, so **it is completely silent**. This is the one true silent-loss-with-`COMPLETED` path found. The field-note customer box had 15 containers.

3. **Phantom domains from commented-out config poison the denominator.** Debian's stock nginx default ships `#	server_name example.com;`, and the harvest has no comment filter. `example.com` entered `sourceDomains`, so the honest score was `1/3`, not `1/4`. Combined with defect 1, **`COMPLETED` is unreachable on essentially any real Debian/Ubuntu source** — a gate that always cries wolf is how a real dark domain ships.

Also worth your attention: the summary tells the customer *"point the DNS, then run certbot"* and *"do not move DNS for these names yet"* about the same hostname (a deadlock); `/home` is silently dropped by `safeCopyTarget` with no report line, and it's in the wizard's own `DEFAULT_PATHS`; and the pre-flight bridged Node **v20.11.1 → v12.22.9 (EOL)** while calling it "the same program."

**Two doc corrections:** `test/migration-gate.test.ts` **does** exist and passes 32/32 — "Known gaps" is stale in the *reassuring* direction. It covers only the extracted pure functions, which is exactly why it caught none of the above: the scorer is correct and is fed corrupted arguments. The stale `migrate.ts` comment at `:5251` is also still there.

I did not touch engine code. One caveat on scope: I drove `runRealMigration` directly rather than through the job queue, since the engine is DB-free — so `migrate.ts:407-417`'s status write was verified by applying its mapping to the real summary, not by a live row update.
